title: Variant Orchestration Playbook Canvas — visual composer for distribution lanes and safety gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a composable canvas inside Redwood Console that lets platform and product engineers author, preview, and validate multi-variant distribution policies (canary, A/B, staged ramp) with safety gates and automated rollback choreography. The canvas should make trade-offs explicit (latency vs. cost vs. quality), enable quick hypothesis creation for experiments, and provide a simulation timeline for expected user exposure before applying policy to live traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas allows creation of at least three variant lanes and assignment of a percentage or rule-based selector to each lane
Interactive safety gate nodes can be attached to lanes (metric thresholds, time windows, hold conditions) and toggled on/off
Preview simulator visualizes a 10-minute and 24-hour distribution timeline with expected request volume and estimated cost delta
Rollback path and compare view show side-by-side variant outputs for the most recent 500 requests (mocked) in the prototype
Prototype accessibility audit completed (keyboard nav, color contrast) and documented remediation tasks
updates: 2026-02-20 — Ticket created by Maya Chen with initial problem statement and draft goals. Linked PRD in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONS/pages/Variant+Orchestration+PRD
2026-02-24 — Kickoff design review with PM (Darren Liu) and Eng lead (Rafa Ortiz). Agreed scope: canvas + simulator + rollback compare. Decision: defer multi-region routing to a follow-up ticket.

2026-02-28 — Low-fi sketches completed and uploaded to shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1VariantCanvasLoFi. Feedback from PM: add explicit cost delta indicator per-lane and option to apply per-token cost model (hosted vs dedicated).

2026-03-03 — Mid-fi Figma prototype created: https://www.figma.com/file/VariantOrch/Playbook-Canvas. Engineering review notes (GitHub issue): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-design/issues/412 — Eng flagged complexity in live-previewing sample requests (KV cache implications).

2026-03-05 — Usability test (6 participants: 3 platform engineers, 3 product PMs). Key findings: users wanted clearer defaults for safety gates, and a more discoverable explainability panel for why rollback was triggered. Action: add inline help and a compact explain panel in the right rail.

2026-03-07 — Design critique with Design Org. Two alternate layouts considered: linear timeline vs. layered swimlanes. Decision: swimlanes offer better quick comparison for A/B scenarios; timeline retained for simulation mode.

2026-03-10 — Accessibility pass started. Found: contrast issues on status chips and keyboard focus missing on lane handles. Created remediation subtasks: DES-51770 (chip contrast) and DES-51771 (lane handle keyboard).

2026-03-12 — Prototype updated with simulated cost estimator and safety-gate templates (latency, error-rate, custom metric). Added rollback compare lane that loads anonymized sample completions for side-by-side diff.

2026-03-14 — Internal PM review: Darren requested an optional 'quick rollback to previous stable' button in top bar and clearer error states when simulator cannot estimate due to missing telemetry. Logged engineering dependency on runtime sampler API: ENG-20688. Planned next: handoff spec and token-level cost modeling with Infra and Runtime teams.
attachments: Related engineering dependency: ENG-20688 (runtime sampler API)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keep canvas affordances minimal to avoid overwhelming new users vs. exposing powerful routing controls for advanced platform teams. We prioritized discoverable templates and progressive disclosure. Simulator uses conservative estimates until runtime telemetry API is available; simulator warns when estimates are low-confidence.
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi visuals, complete accessibility fixes, create final handoff package (components, tokens, interactions) and schedule a joint design+eng spec review on 2026-03-18. Coordinate with ENG-20688 for sampler integration and with PM to define experiment measurement events.
notes_for_engineering: Prototype includes interactive JS-based simulator; engineering should review complexity of hooking to runtime sampler. Provide API contract for sample request playback (500-sample limit) and cost model inputs. Consider fallbacks for air-gapped/private deployments where telemetry may be delayed.
final_decision: TBD — waiting on runtime sampler feasibility and a final tradeoff review.
